entries.title: How to Play Chess with Yourself
entries.description: The First Textbook of the School. Sixteen short chapters on noticing before naming, reading the grammar and stories underneath what we say, and treating life as a long game of chess played with yourself rather than against the world.

entries.title: How to Play on the Emotional Chessboard
entries.description: The Second Tome, and a companion to the first. Reading the invisible boards inside every room, conversation and organisation: the emotional pieces, opening theory and endgames, political literacy, the patterns of manipulation, and harmony as the aim rather than victory.

entries.title: The Emotional Chessboard
entries.description: A model for staying deliberate under emotional pressure: treat feeling and position as a board you can read, rather than weather that happens to you.

entries.title: The More Powerful the Instrument
entries.description: The founding argument of the School. As instruments get stronger, the judgement of the person holding them becomes the scarce and decisive part.

entries.title: Reading the Instrument
entries.description: A short checklist for looking at a piece of media and asking what made it, who aimed it, and what it wants from you.

entries.title: Signal and Noise
entries.description: Noise is not the absence of signal; it is signal you have not yet learned to read. A working note on filtering without discarding.

entries.title: On Generated Artifacts
entries.description: What a generated image, sentence, or plan actually is — a dense average of prior work — and how to hold one responsibly.

entries.title: The Responsibility to Say Something
entries.description: Fluency is now cheap. Having something to say, and meaning it, is the part that did not get automated.
